technique: CT head without contrast, 5 mm axial acquisitions.
findings: Prominent cortical sulci and enlarged lateral ventricles, out of proportion to the sulcal widening at the high convexity. Periventricular and deep white matter hypodensities consistent with chronic small vessel ischaemic change. A 6 mm lacunar hypodensity in the right caudate head, consistent with an old lacunar infarct. No haemorrhage, mass or acute extra-axial collection.
impression: Ventricular enlargement out of proportion to sulcal atrophy, which may represent normal pressure hydrocephalus in the appropriate clinical setting. Chronic small vessel ischaemic change and an old right caudate lacune. No acute intracranial abnormality.
